bibliography.note: Curry, R. A., Currie, S. L., Arndt, S. K. & Bielak, A. T., Environmental Biology of Fishes 72(2): 111–122 (February 2005), title as cited

claims.claim: at New Brunswick's northern range limit, age-0 fish sheltered in gaps in the substrate below about 10 °C and were mostly in water under 3 m by autumn (cited 'via a secondary source')
under ice in northern New Brunswick, young smallmouth under 50 mm died
claims.note: the abstract summary seen agrees that fish under 50 mm TL appeared to die under the ice; it also reports that in lake enclosures smaller fish survived better as exposure temperature rose and the largest fish worse

claims.claim: survivors lost 22–54 % of their ash-free dry weight
claims.note: the abstract summary seen gives 22–54 % of pre-winter energy reserves as ash-free dry weight, similar to wild fish caught in spring

claims.claim: the cold-respiration curve's juvenile end is set from 'Curry 2005's YOY depletion' (field depletion of 30–55 mg O₂ kg⁻¹ h⁻¹ for YOY at 2–6 °C, species.js:362–363)
